seo.title: DeFi Security Checklist for Developers
seo.description: A comprehensive security checklist for DeFi developers covering AMMs, lending, vaults, and cross-protocol integrations. Ship secure DeFi code.

content.intro: DeFi protocols handle significant value and face sophisticated attackers. Use this checklist to ensure your protocol is hardened against known attack vectors before deployment.

sections.heading: Oracle Security
sections.description: Protect against price manipulation and oracle failures.

items.title: Use TWAP or manipulation-resistant oracles
items.description: Avoid spot prices from DEXes. Use Chainlink, time-weighted averages, or other manipulation-resistant sources.

items.title: Implement oracle staleness checks
items.description: Reject prices older than acceptable threshold. Include updatedAt timestamp validation.

items.title: Add oracle fallback mechanisms
items.description: If primary oracle fails, have a secondary source or safe fallback behavior.

items.title: Validate oracle price bounds
items.description: Reject prices that deviate too far from expected ranges to catch oracle manipulation.

items.title: Check oracle decimals handling
items.description: Chainlink feeds have different decimals. Normalize all price feeds to consistent precision.

items.title: Protect against oracle front-running
items.description: Consider commit-reveal or other mechanisms if oracle updates create arbitrage opportunities.

items.title: Use TWAP instead of spot prices
items.description: Flash loans cannot manipulate time-weighted averages. Never rely on single-block spot prices.

items.title: Add deposit/withdraw delays where needed
items.description: For governance or rewards, consider requiring deposits to be present for multiple blocks.

items.title: Check same-block deposit-and-action restrictions
items.description: Prevent users from depositing and taking action (voting, claiming) in the same block.

items.title: Validate share price manipulation resistance
items.description: Vault share prices should not be manipulable by large deposits/withdrawals in single transactions.

items.title: Consider flash loan fees in arbitrage calculations
items.description: Understand that attackers pay fees. Some attacks are unprofitable after fees.

items.title: Verify constant product/sum invariant maintained
items.description: After every operation, the pool invariant must hold. Test edge cases thoroughly.

items.title: Protect against sandwich attacks
items.description: Implement slippage protection and consider private transaction submission options.

items.title: Check minimum liquidity requirements
items.description: First LP should lock minimum liquidity to prevent share price manipulation.

items.title: Validate fee calculation accuracy
items.description: Fees must be calculated correctly in all scenarios including edge cases.

items.title: Test imbalanced pool scenarios
items.description: Verify behavior when pools become highly imbalanced or near-empty.

items.title: Check LP token mint/burn accounting
items.description: LP tokens must accurately represent share of pool. No inflation or deflation bugs.

items.title: Verify health factor calculations
items.description: Health factor must be calculated correctly including all positions and proper oracle prices.

items.title: Check liquidation thresholds and incentives
items.description: Liquidation must be profitable enough to incentivize liquidators but not excessive.

items.title: Protect against bad debt scenarios
items.description: Have mechanisms to handle underwater positions where debt exceeds collateral.

items.title: Verify interest rate model
items.description: Interest accrual must be calculated correctly. Test with various utilization levels.

items.title: Check borrow cap enforcement
items.description: Borrow limits must be enforced to prevent protocol insolvency.

items.title: Test partial liquidation scenarios
items.description: Partial liquidations must leave positions in valid state or fully liquidate.

sections.heading: Vault and Yield Security
sections.description: For vaults, yield aggregators, and staking.

items.title: Protect against first depositor attack
items.description: Send small amount to vault on deployment or implement virtual shares to prevent share inflation attack.

items.title: Validate share price calculations
items.description: Share price must accurately reflect underlying assets. Check for rounding attacks.

items.title: Check donation attack resistance
items.description: Donating tokens to vault should not unfairly benefit or harm depositors.

items.title: Verify withdrawal queue handling
items.description: If using withdrawal queues, ensure fair processing and no front-running.

items.title: Check yield strategy risks
items.description: Understand and document risks of underlying yield sources. Implement loss limits.

items.title: Implement emergency withdrawal
items.description: Users should be able to withdraw in emergencies even if it means forfeiting some yield.

sections.heading: Token Integration Security
sections.description: Handle edge cases with various token implementations.

items.title: Use SafeERC20 for all token transfers
items.description: Some tokens don't return bool. SafeERC20 handles these edge cases.

items.title: Handle fee-on-transfer tokens
items.description: Calculate actual received amount after transfer, not the transfer amount.

items.title: Handle rebasing tokens
items.description: Account for balance changes between transactions for tokens like stETH.

items.title: Check token decimal handling
items.description: Normalize calculations for tokens with different decimals (USDC has 6, DAI has 18).

items.title: Verify approval patterns
items.description: Use increaseAllowance/decreaseAllowance or reset to zero first for tokens with approval race conditions.

items.title: Handle tokens with blocklists
items.description: USDC and USDT can blocklist addresses. Consider implications for your protocol.

sections.heading: Economic Security
sections.description: Protect against economic exploits and incentive manipulation.

items.title: Model economic attacks
items.description: Think through how an attacker with unlimited capital could exploit your protocol.

items.title: Verify fee and reward math
items.description: All fee distributions must sum correctly. No funds should be lost or created.

items.title: Check for MEV extraction opportunities
items.description: Identify where sandwich attacks, front-running, or back-running could harm users.

items.title: Validate incentive alignment
items.description: Ensure all protocol participants are incentivized to behave honestly.

items.title: Test extreme market conditions
items.description: Simulate behavior during high volatility, black swan events, and market crashes.

proTips.tip: Always get an audit before mainnet deployment. DeFi protocols are high-value targets.
Study past exploits deeply. Most new exploits are variations of known attack patterns.
Deploy to mainnet with limited caps first. Increase limits as the protocol proves itself.
Set up monitoring and alerts for unusual activity. Early detection limits damage.
Have an incident response plan ready before you need it. Know who to call and what to do.
